lines.japanese: 放課後。
lines.english: After school.

lines.japanese: 昨日の会議でクラスのみんなに声をかけてはみたものの、結果は予想していた通りだった。
lines.english: I had tried asking everyone in class at yesterday’s meeting, but the result was exactly what I had expected.

lines.japanese: 僕は誰もいない教室でひとり、職員室から借りてきた、ここ何年かの卒業文集を調べていた。
lines.english: Alone in the empty classroom, I studied the graduation anthologies from the past several years that I had borrowed from the faculty room.

lines.japanese: 「ふぅー……」
lines.english: “Whew...”

lines.japanese: ぱらぱらと開いてみても、なにを参考にすればいいのかよく分からない。こういうものは、最初に全体の構想をまとめるべきなのか、順を追って徐々に固めていくべきなのか。
lines.english: However many pages I flipped through, I could not tell what I was supposed to learn from them. Were you meant to begin with a plan for the whole thing, or work in order and let it gradually take shape?

lines.japanese: 生徒たちが原稿用紙に手書きで提出したはずの文章は、すべて画一的な活字に変わって整然と並んでいる。なんとなく手書きの文字が恋しくなって、ページをどんどん飛ばしていった。
lines.english: The essays the students must have submitted in their own handwriting had all been converted into uniform type and set out in orderly rows. I found myself missing handwritten words, and began skipping rapidly ahead.

lines.japanese: ようやく温かみのあるページに行きあたった。制作班長の名前を中央に、関わったスタッフが一言ずつ寄せ書きしている。文集のあとがきみたいだ。
lines.english: At last I came upon a page with some warmth to it. The production leader’s name stood in the center, surrounded by a few words from each member of the staff. It was like an afterword to the anthology.

lines.japanese: 「みんなをまとめてくれた委員長にはマジ感謝してます！　一年間お疲れさま！」
lines.english: “Huge thanks to our class rep for keeping us all together! Great work this year!”

lines.japanese: 「うちらの友情は永遠！　みんなで蜃気楼の彼方へミラージュララバイ！」
lines.english: “Our friendship is forever! Together, beyond the mirage—Mirage Lullaby!”

lines.japanese: 「大変だったけど、出来上がったときには素で涙でました。きっと俺たちは羽ばたける！」
lines.english: “It was rough, but when we finished, I honestly cried. I know we can spread our wings!”

lines.japanese: この寄せ書きだけ見ると、製作者たちが放課後に集まって楽しそうに作業している姿が目に浮かぶ。
lines.english: Judging by these messages alone, I could picture the production team gathering after school and happily working together.

lines.japanese: 僕たちも建前だけはこんな風に感謝し合ったりするんだろうか。
lines.english: Would we end up exchanging thanks like these too, if only for appearance’s sake?

lines.japanese: そもそも完成するかどうかも怪しいけれど。
lines.english: It was doubtful whether we would finish at all.

lines.japanese: 大して作業もしていないのになんだか疲れてしまい、携帯電話を取りだして開いてみた。届いてるメールは１件。ハンバーガー屋のメールマガジン。
lines.english: Though I had hardly done any work, I somehow felt tired. I took out my phone and opened it. One new message: a promotional email from a hamburger place.

lines.japanese: かちかち弄りながら、帰ろうかな、なんて思ったりもした。だけど、何かの用事で教室に戻ってきたひとが、誰もいない教室を見たらどう思うだろう。
lines.english: As I clicked idly through my phone, I wondered whether I should go home. But what if someone returned to the classroom on an errand and found nobody here? What would they think?

lines.japanese: 僕は机に向きなおって、資料閲覧という名の作業を再開した。
lines.english: I turned back to the desk and resumed what I was calling research.

lines.japanese: 今日はグレタガルドからの召喚はかからないんだろうか。今なら時間にも余裕があるってのに。
lines.english: Was there going to be no summons from Gretagard today? For once, I actually had time to spare.

lines.japanese: そう願いながらぼんやりとしていると、少しずつ頭に靄がかかってきた。ああ、もしかしてこれは……。
lines.english: As I sat there wishing for one, a haze slowly gathered in my mind. Ah. Could this be...?

lines.japanese: 金色の粒子が世界を染めあげる。どこからか福音の鐘が聞こえてくるようだ。
lines.english: Golden motes suffused the world. I could almost hear bells of glad tidings ringing somewhere.

lines.japanese: ああ、そうだ。早くあの世界へ行かないと。また冒険の続きを始めなくちゃ――
lines.english: Yes. I had to hurry back to that world. I had to resume my adventure—

lines.japanese: ガチャッ
lines.english: Clack.

lines.japanese: 意識を引きもどすように、乾いた現実の音がした。
lines.english: A dry sound from the real world dragged me back to myself.

lines.japanese: 途端に金色の粒子は霧消し、はっきりと視界が開ける。ここは教室だ。
lines.english: The golden motes vanished at once, and my vision cleared. I was in the classroom.

lines.japanese: 振りかえると、針生さんが後ろのドアから入ってきた。まとわりつく空気すら鬱陶しそうに見える、いつもの表情だ。
lines.english: I turned to see Hariu entering through the rear door, wearing his usual expression, as though even the air clinging to him were an intolerable nuisance.

lines.japanese: 班員が現れてくれたことに僕は淡い喜びを覚えた。
lines.english: A faint joy stirred in me at the sight of another group member.

lines.japanese: 「針生さん、来てくれたんですか」
lines.english: “Hariu, did you come to help?”

lines.japanese: 「いや、忘れ物」
lines.english: “No. Forgot something.”

lines.japanese: 現実は冷たかった。それはそうだ。きのう針生さんは、形だけの参加ときっぱり言いきっている。
lines.english: Reality was cold. Of course it was. Hariu had made it perfectly clear yesterday that he was participating in name only.

lines.japanese: 彼は自分の机の引きだしから教科書を引っぱりだしていた。ふとさっきの文集で見た言葉がよぎる。そうだ、僕たちも羽ばたける。
lines.english: He pulled a textbook from his desk. A phrase from the anthology crossed my mind. That was right. We could spread our wings too.
“Um—”

lines.japanese: 「あん？」
lines.english: “Huh?”
“Dams...”

lines.japanese: 「ダム、いいですよね。針生さんに勧められたから、昨日ちょっとだけネットでダムを調べてみたんです」
lines.english: “Dams are wonderful, aren't they? You recommended them, so I looked them up online yesterday.”

lines.japanese: 「画像見てるだけでも面白いですけど、文字資料を読みだしたら本当あっという間に時間が過ぎちゃって。奥が深いんですね」
lines.english: “Even the pictures are interesting, but once I started reading the articles, the time just vanished. There’s so much to them.”

lines.japanese: 「はン」
lines.english: “Hah.”

lines.japanese: 針生さんは僕の目的を見透かしたように鼻を鳴らした。
lines.english: Hariu snorted as though he had seen straight through me.

lines.japanese: 「マメだな、おまえ」
lines.english: “You’re thorough, I’ll give you that.”

lines.japanese: 「昨日言ったよなァ、参加するのは形だけでいいって。俺は内申点なんかどうだっていいんだ、卒業にも興味ねえしな。無駄なことに時間を割く暇はないんだよ。おまえも嫌だったら、そんなもんやらなきゃいいだろ」
lines.english: “I told you yesterday, didn’t I? I’m only in the group on paper. I couldn’t care less about my school record, and I’m not interested in graduating either. I don’t have time to waste on pointless crap. If you hate doing it too, then don’t.”
“What...?”

lines.japanese: 返す言葉が見つからなかった。針生さんはただ子供みたいに我儘を言ってるだけじゃなくて、相応の覚悟をしているみたいだ。
lines.english: I could think of nothing to say. Hariu was not simply behaving like a selfish child. He seemed fully prepared to accept the consequences.

lines.japanese: 僕だって卒業できるか分かったものじゃない。でも彼みたいに周囲を敵にまわす度胸はなかった。その程度の臆病者に、彼を責める権利はないのかもしれない。そう、それだ。
lines.english: I had no guarantee I would graduate either. But I lacked his nerve to turn everyone around me into an enemy. A coward like me might have no right to condemn him. Yes. That was it.

lines.japanese: 「あの、すみませ……こふ、こふっ」
lines.english: “Um, I’m sor—cough, cough.”

lines.japanese: うまく喋れなかった。喉が渇く。針生さんがミネラルウォーターのペットボトルを咥えた。一口もらえないかと本気で思った。
lines.english: The words would not come out properly. My throat was dry. Hariu put a bottle of mineral water to his lips, and for one earnest moment I hoped he might give me a sip.

lines.japanese: 「まァ、ダムに関しちゃ──」
lines.english: “As for dams—”
“Yes?”

lines.japanese: 「──きっかけはどうあれ、趣味を広げンのはいいことだ。面白いもんはそこら中に転がってるよ、目ん玉かっぴろげて青春しなよチェリーボーイ」
lines.english: “Whatever got you started, it’s good to broaden your interests. There’s interesting stuff everywhere. Open those eyes of yours and go have some fun while you’re young, you virgin.”

lines.japanese: 針生さんはペットボトルのキャップを締めながらそう言った。口元に笑み。僕は安堵した。救いようがないほど嫌われているわけじゃないのかもしれない。
lines.english: Hariu said this while screwing the cap back onto his bottle, a smile at the corner of his mouth. Relief washed over me. Perhaps he did not hate me beyond all hope.

lines.japanese: 「あの、今日はもう時間残ってませんか」
lines.english: “Um, do you have any time left today?”

lines.japanese: 喉が渇いていたけど、唾を飲みこんでなんとか声を出してみた。やってみればすんなりと声は出た。
lines.english: My throat was dry, but I swallowed and forced the words out. Once I tried, they came surprisingly easily.

lines.japanese: 「ン？　ダムの話か？」
lines.english: “Hm? Is this about dams?”

lines.japanese: 「いえ、卒業文集のことで。時間があれば相談だけでも乗ってもらえれば」
lines.english: “No, about the graduation anthology. If you have time, I was hoping I could at least ask your advice.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、ダムの話も聞きたいですけど」
lines.english: “Though I'd like to hear more about dams too.”

lines.japanese: 気が付いて付けくわえた。針生さんはきょろきょろ見回しながら眼鏡のブリッジを押さえた。
lines.english: I remembered to add that. Hariu pressed a finger to the bridge of his glasses and glanced restlessly around the room.

lines.japanese: 「ダムはもう古い」
lines.english: “Dams are old news.”
“What?”

lines.japanese: 「いまはなァ、仏像だよ仏像」
lines.english: “These days it’s Buddhist statues. Buddhist statues.”

lines.japanese: 「ぶつぞう？」
lines.english: “Buddhist statues?”

lines.japanese: 「おまえ、一木と寄木だとどっちが好き？」
lines.english: “Which do you like better, single-block or joined-block carving?”

lines.japanese: 唐突すぎてびっくりした。
lines.english: The question was so abrupt that it startled me.

lines.japanese: 「さ、さあ……すみません、おれにはちょっと分かりません」
lines.english: “I-I don't know... I'm sorry. I don't really understand the difference.”

lines.japanese: 「選択、日本史じゃねーの」
lines.english: “Didn’t you choose Japanese history?”

lines.japanese: あ、そういえば聞き覚えぐらいはあったような……
lines.english: Oh. Now that he mentioned it, the terms did sound vaguely familiar...

lines.japanese: 「え、っと、たしか一木造は平安初期までで……寄木はそれ以降の主流……でしたっけ」
lines.english: “Um... if I remember right, single-block statues were made up through the early Heian period, and joined-block construction became the standard after that... didn’t it?”

lines.japanese: 間違ってるかもしれない。でも無回答よりはましだ。間違いなら指摘してもらえる。少しは針生さんの話に付いていけるかもしれない。
lines.english: I might have been wrong. But an answer was better than silence; if I was wrong, he could correct me. Perhaps then I could follow at least a little of what Hariu was saying.

lines.japanese: 「やっぱ一木に憧れるよなァ。俺もどっかの神木使って仏像造りてえなあ。おまえだったらなに彫る？　不動明王とかベタだもんねェ。俺なァ、軍荼利明王流行らせたいんだよ。あいつ一番ロックでしょう」
lines.english: “You’ve got to admire single-block carving, though. I’d love to get hold of some sacred tree and carve a statue myself. What would you carve? Fudo? He’s the obvious Wisdom King. Me, I want Gundari to catch on. He’s the most rock-and-roll of the lot.”

lines.japanese: 無理だった。
lines.english: I was out of my depth.

lines.japanese: 「すみません、やっぱりおれには分かりません」
lines.english: “I'm sorry. I still don't understand.”

lines.japanese: 「あァ、まァ、そういうわけだ。今日も近所の寺巡りだから。お先」
lines.english: “Ah, well. Anyway, that’s why I’m making the rounds of the neighborhood temples again today. See you.”

lines.japanese: 「いい仏様が見つかるといいですね」
lines.english: “I hope you find a good one.”

lines.japanese: 「そうだなァ、なかなかねえんだよなァ」
lines.english: “Yeah. They’re not easy to find.”

lines.japanese: 針生さんは泳ぐように去っていった。
lines.english: Hariu drifted away as though swimming.

lines.japanese: ひとりに戻ったあと、ケータイから仏像に関するサイトを探してみた。いくつか巡ってみると、思ったより面白かった。
lines.english: Once I was alone again, I used my phone to look up websites about Buddhist statues. After browsing a few, I found the subject more interesting than I had expected.

lines.japanese: それからしばらく、一人で作業を続けた。作業と言っても、過去の文集を読みあさるだけだけれど。
lines.english: Then I went on working alone for a while—though the ‘work’ amounted to reading through old anthologies.

lines.japanese: それでも目を通す前よりは、何をするべきか形は見えてきた。気がする。具体的な作業工程がビジョンとして浮かんできた。気がする。
lines.english: Even so, I had a better idea of what needed doing than before. I thought. A concrete vision of the process was beginning to take shape. I thought.

lines.japanese: ふられたばかりなのに、もし針生さんが手伝ってくれるならこの係をお願いしよう、なんて図々しく役割分担まで考えてしまう。
lines.english: Although he had just turned me down, I was brazen enough to start imagining which job I would give Hariu if he ever agreed to help.

lines.japanese: でもそんなことを考えるのも、今の僕にとっては格段に楽しい作業だ。なんだかノッてきた、次は四年前のクラス写真か……。
lines.english: But even thinking about that made the work far more enjoyable than it had been. I was getting into it now. Next came the class photographs from four years ago...

lines.japanese: 「よかった、まだいた」
lines.english: “Good. You're still here.”
“What?”

lines.japanese: 前のドアが開いて、コンビニ袋を提げた女子がひとり。
lines.english: The front door opened, revealing a girl carrying a convenience-store bag.

lines.japanese: 「ごめん、遅れて。飲まなきゃやってられないと思って、ひとっ走り行ってきました班長」
lines.english: “Sorry I’m late, group leader. I figured we’d need drinks to get through this, so I made a quick run.”

lines.japanese: びっくりした。彼女はとっくに帰ったと思ってた。
lines.english: I was astonished. I had assumed she had gone home long ago.

lines.japanese: 学校から一番近いコンビニのレジ袋を、手に高々と掲げている。
lines.english: She held a plastic bag from the nearest convenience store triumphantly aloft.

lines.japanese: 「え……渡来さん、どうしてここに」
lines.english: “Watarai...? Why are you here?”

lines.japanese: 「どうしてって。なにそれ。羽田班の仕事に、羽田班の私が参加するのは当たり前じゃない？」
lines.english: “What do you mean, why? I’m in the Haneda group. Of course I’d help with the Haneda group’s work.”

lines.japanese: 「そう、だけど……」
lines.english: “Yes, but...”

lines.japanese: でも当たり前じゃないのが当たり前なんて、僕にはよくあることだから。
lines.english: But in my life, it was perfectly ordinary for the obvious not to happen.

lines.japanese: どさっ。
lines.english: Thump.

lines.japanese: 目の前にビニール袋が降ってきた。開いていたページは白いポリエチレンに潰されて見えなくなった。
lines.english: The plastic bag landed in front of me. Its white polyethylene smothered the open pages and hid them from sight.

lines.japanese: 「ハイ、差し入れ。お代はいいよ、そのかーし今度の買い出しんときは羽田君持ちってことで」
lines.english: “Here, refreshments. You don't have to pay me back—provided you cover the next supply run.”

lines.japanese: 「うん、分かった。ありがとう」
lines.english: “All right. Thank you.”

lines.japanese: 僕は泣きだしたい気持ちでコンビニ袋を覗きこんだ。数本のペットボトルとスナック菓子が入ってる。その中から渡来さんが微炭酸の林檎ソーダを取りだした。
lines.english: I felt like bursting into tears as I peered into the bag. Inside were several plastic bottles and bags of snacks. Watarai took out a lightly carbonated apple soda.

lines.japanese: 「世界は金色に包まれているのだー」
lines.english: “The world is bathed in gold!”

lines.japanese: 「意味が分からないよ」
lines.english: “I have no idea what that means.”

lines.japanese: でも僕は笑った。意味が分からなくても、とても笑いたくなったからだ。
lines.english: But I laughed. Even without understanding what she meant, I wanted to laugh so badly.

lines.japanese: 「まあ、私じゃなくて、友達がそんなこと言ってたんだ」
lines.english: “Well, it wasn’t me. A friend of mine said something like that.”

lines.japanese: 渡来さんはビニール袋から紙コップをふたつ取りだして、それぞれにアップルソーダを注いだ。
lines.english: Watarai took two paper cups from the bag and filled each with apple soda.

lines.japanese: 「はい」
lines.english: “Here.”

lines.japanese: 「え？　ああ」
lines.english: “What? Oh.”

lines.japanese: 注がれたコップを持ちあげて、その端をこつん。世間でいうところの「お疲れさま」だ。
lines.english: I raised the cup she had filled and tapped its rim against hers. It was the gesture people used to say “good work.”

lines.japanese: 「やっぱり針生先輩は来ないか。じゃあ班長ひとりで作業してたんだ。偉いね」
lines.english: “So Hariu didn’t come after all. You’ve been working here all by yourself, group leader. That’s impressive.”

lines.japanese: 「そんなことないよ。昔の文集見てただけだし」
lines.english: “Not really. I’ve only been looking through old anthologies.”

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ全然偉くないね」
lines.english: “Then that’s not impressive at all.”
“Haha...”

lines.japanese: 「でもやっぱり偉いよ」
lines.english: “No, you still are.”

lines.japanese: 「ありがとう」
lines.english: “Thank you.”

lines.japanese: 渡来さんはジュースを一気に呷ると、もう一度自分の紙コップに二杯目を注いだ。
lines.english: Watarai drained her drink in one gulp, then poured herself a second cup.

lines.japanese: 「ていうか、ほとんど押しつけられちゃって悔しくない？」
lines.english: “Seriously, though, doesn’t it make you mad that they dumped almost all of it on you?”

lines.japanese: 「え、なんのこと……？」
lines.english: “What do you mean...?”

lines.japanese: 「昨日の会議の内容」
lines.english: “Yesterday's meeting.”

lines.japanese: 「実質、ほとんど全部の作業が私たちの担当、ってことになっちゃったでしょ」
lines.english: “Practically all the work ended up being assigned to us, remember?”

lines.japanese: 「高内とかみんなで私たちに仕事押しつけちゃって。これって羽田班に対する冒涜だよ。班長、ちょっとシメてこい」
lines.english: “Takauchi and the others dumped it all on us. This is an insult to the Haneda group. Group leader, go teach them a lesson.”

lines.japanese: 可愛いのも格好いいのも、渡来さんはどっちだって様になるんだ。まぶしいなあ。
lines.english: Cute or cool, Watarai could carry off either one. She was dazzling.

lines.japanese: 「はは、違うんだよ渡来さん。そもそも昨日の会議は高内さんが開いてくれたものなんだ」
lines.english: “Haha. You've misunderstood, Watarai. Takauchi was the one who arranged yesterday's meeting in the first place.”
“Hm?”

lines.japanese: 「おれは自分で議事進行をするって言いだしたのに、まとめきれなかったし。だからその分の責任を取るのは当然のことで。むしろ高内さんには、謝らなきゃいけないぐらいなんだ」
lines.english: “I volunteered to run the meeting myself, and then I failed to bring the discussion together. It’s only right that I take responsibility for that. If anything, I should apologize to Takauchi.”

lines.japanese: 「ん？　んん？」
lines.english: “Hm? Hmmm?”

lines.japanese: 「だから、おれのせいで渡来さんや針生さんを巻きこむのは申しわけなくて。今日はありがとう。でも明日からはおれひとりでやるから、もう大丈夫だよ」
lines.english: “So I feel terrible for dragging you and Hariu into a problem I caused. Thank you for today. But I’ll do it alone from tomorrow on, so you don’t have to worry anymore.”

lines.japanese: 昨日のことを思いかえすと、自分の行動が恥ずかしく思えてきた。羞恥のせいか自然に手の力が入って、紙コップがペコリと軽く潰れる音がした。
lines.english: Thinking back on yesterday, I began to feel ashamed of how I had behaved. My hand tightened of its own accord, and the paper cup gave a soft pop as it crumpled slightly.

lines.japanese: 「んんー？　なんか……ぜんぜん納得できない論理展開だよね」
lines.english: “Hmmm? Somehow... I don’t find that reasoning convincing at all.”

lines.japanese: 「そうかな。じゃあたぶん、おれの説明が下手なんだ。ごめん」
lines.english: “Really? Then I probably explained it badly. I'm sorry.”

lines.japanese: 「わ、謝っちゃった」
lines.english: “Wow. He apologized.”

lines.japanese: 渡来さんは両てのひらを顔の横に置いて、大袈裟に身を引いた。愉快なのまで様になるんだ。
lines.english: Watarai raised both palms beside her face and recoiled theatrically. Even playing the fool looked good on her.

lines.japanese: 「つまり羽田君は、いまの状況にまったく不満を感じていないと？」
lines.english: “So what you’re saying is that you have absolutely no complaints about the situation?”

lines.japanese: 「不満っていうか、やっぱり不安みたいなのはあるけど……学級委員長だから仕方ないんじゃないかな」
lines.english: “I wouldn’t call it dissatisfaction. I am worried, of course... but I’m the class representative, so I suppose it can’t be helped.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、そういえば、その学級委員長もなかば無理矢理やらされた感じだったよね」
lines.english: “Oh, yes. Come to think of it, you were more or less forced into being class representative too.”

lines.japanese: 「誰かがやらなきゃならないことだから、みんなが嫌がることならおれがやればいいんだよ。ひとりでも誰かが喜んでくれるなら、それでおれも嬉しい気持ちになれるし」
lines.english: “Someone has to do it. If everyone else hates the job, I might as well be the one to take it. And if it makes even one person happy, that makes me happy too.”

lines.japanese: 「そっかー」
lines.english: “I see.”

lines.japanese: 渡来さんは僕のへこんだ紙コップにとくとく注ぎたしてくれた。
lines.english: Watarai poured more soda into my dented paper cup with a gentle glug-glug.

lines.japanese: 「羽田君の想像力はすごいなあ。物事の良し悪しなんて、結局は考え方次第なのかもしれないね」
lines.english: “You have an amazing imagination, Haneda. Maybe whether something is good or bad really does depend on how you choose to see it.”

lines.japanese: 「そうかな。うん、そうかもね」
lines.english: “You think? Yeah, maybe you’re right.”

lines.japanese: 「ふーん、なるほどだー」
lines.english: “Hmm. I see how it is.”

lines.japanese: 渡来さんは同じソーダをもう一本袋の中から取りだすと、ラベルをはがして自分の目の前にかざした。
lines.english: Watarai took another bottle of the same soda from the bag, peeled off the label, and held it up before her eyes.

lines.japanese: 「ほーら、ごらん。これだけで世界が金色に輝いてしまうぞう」
lines.english: “See? Just like that, the whole world shines gold!”

lines.japanese: 「あれ、馬鹿にしてる？」
lines.english: “Wait. Are you making fun of me?”

lines.japanese: 「えっ、まさか。面白いひとだなって」
lines.english: “What? Of course not. I was thinking what an interesting person you are.”

lines.japanese: 「羽田君も面白いと思うよ」
lines.english: “I think you're pretty interesting yourself.”

lines.japanese: 「ありがとう。そんなこと言われたの久しぶりだよ」
lines.english: “Thank you. It’s been a long time since anyone said that about me.”

lines.japanese: 「羽田君って、ナチュラルに世界が金色に見えてそうだよね」
lines.english: “You seem like the kind of person who sees the world through a golden glow without even trying, Haneda.”

lines.japanese: 「そうかな。うん、でも、渡来さんが言うならそうかもね」
lines.english: “You think so? Yeah, well, if you say so, maybe I am.”

lines.japanese: 「この世界が金色なのかな。それとも羽田君の目に金色のフィルターが付いてるのかな」
lines.english: “I wonder if the world itself is golden, or if your eyes have a golden filter over them.”

lines.japanese: 「ていうか、金色に見えるのはいいことなのかな、悪いことなのかな」
lines.english: “But is seeing everything in gold a good thing or a bad thing?”

lines.japanese: 「それとも、こことは別のところに金色の世界はあるのかもしれない」
lines.english: “Or perhaps the golden world exists somewhere else entirely.”

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ羽田君は、もしそういうところがあったら行きたい？」
lines.english: “If such a place existed, would you want to go there?”

lines.japanese: 渡来さんがジュースを差しだしてくる。だけど僕はそれを受けとらなかった。
lines.english: Watarai offered me the soda, but I did not take it.

lines.japanese: 「ううん、しばらくは必要ないかな」
lines.english: “No. I don’t think I’ll need any for a while.”

lines.japanese: 「えっ」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: 「あ。えっと、そじゃなくて、ジュースの話」
lines.english: “Oh. Um, I meant the soda, not that.”

lines.japanese: 渡来さんは不思議そうな顔をしたけど、すぐに笑顔を浮かべて自分のコップに林檎ソーダを注いだ。
lines.english: Watarai looked puzzled, but soon smiled and poured the apple soda into her own cup.

lines.japanese: 「羽田君、学校は楽しい？」
lines.english: “Haneda, do you enjoy school?”

lines.japanese: 「学校は楽しむところじゃないよ。でも最近ちょっと好きになってきたかも」
lines.english: “School isn’t a place you go to have fun. But lately I might have started liking it a little.”

lines.japanese: 「ほんと？　なんで？」
lines.english: “Really? Why?”

lines.japanese: 渡来さんのおかげだよ。
lines.english: Because of you.

lines.japanese: 「理由はとくにないと思う。おれが変わったんじゃなくて、世界が変わったんじゃないかな」
lines.english: “I don’t think there’s any particular reason. Maybe I’m not the one who changed. Maybe the world did.”

lines.japanese: 「渡来さんはどう、学校は」
lines.english: “What about you, Watarai? How do you feel about school?”

lines.japanese: 「私か……私は……」
「私もそんな感じかな」
lines.english: “I guess I feel the same way.”

lines.japanese: 「いままで授業も部活も人付き合いも、なんかかったるーいって感じだったけど、最近ちょっと目標っていうか、やり甲斐のある仕事を見つけて、ちょっと燃えてきたところ」
lines.english: “Until recently, classes, clubs, dealing with people—it all felt like such a pain. But now I’ve found something like a goal. A job worth doing. I’m starting to get fired up.”

lines.japanese: 「いいな。どんな仕事」
lines.english: “That sounds nice. What kind of job?”

lines.japanese: 「うーん、人助け？」
lines.english: “Hmm. Helping someone?”

lines.japanese: 「あ……もしかしてそれって……」
lines.english: “Oh... Could that be...?”
“What?”

lines.japanese: 「この卒文制作のこと？」
lines.english: “The graduation anthology?”

lines.japanese: 「あー」
lines.english: “Ah.”

lines.japanese: 「うん、じゃあ当面それで」
lines.english: “Sure. Let’s go with that for now.”

lines.japanese: 「ありがとう。渡来さんってすごく優しいんだね」
lines.english: “Thank you. You’re really kind, Watarai.”

lines.japanese: 「どうなんだろ。余計なお世話なのかもしれないけど、でも最後にはありがとうって言ってもらえたらちょっと嬉しいよね」
lines.english: “I don’t know. Maybe I’m only meddling where I’m not wanted. But if someone thanks me at the end, that does feel kind of nice.”

lines.japanese: 「言うよもちろん。ありがとう」
lines.english: “Of course I'll thank you. Thank you.”

lines.japanese: 「あいあい。さて、それじゃ残りの時間で出来ることやっちゃおっか。ね、班長」
lines.english: “Aye, aye. All right, let’s do what we can with the time we’ve got left, group leader.”

lines.japanese: 渡来さんは両手をばんざいしながらすとんと自分の椅子に座ると、机の上に手を伸ばした。
lines.english: Watarai flung both hands overhead, dropped neatly into her chair, and reached across the desk.

lines.japanese: 暖房の効いた教室内の空気で多少ぬるくなってはいたけれど、林檎ソーダは夕焼けを反射してしゅわしゅわと輝いて見えた。
lines.english: The heated classroom had warmed the apple soda a little, but it caught the sunset and seemed to glitter as it fizzed.

lines.japanese: 渡来さんと二人だけの時間。世界は金色に包まれていた。
lines.english: Time alone with Watarai. The world was bathed in gold.

lines.japanese: 「あ、そうだ。今日はどうかな」
lines.english: “Oh, right. How about today?”
“Hm?”

lines.japanese: 二人で作業を始めてから、担任が覗き程度に顔を出して「もう帰りなさい」と言われるくらいに時間が過ぎた。
lines.english: We had been working together long enough for our homeroom teacher to poke her head in and tell us to go home.

lines.japanese: 片付けをしていたら渡来さんが何かを思いだしたように僕の前に立っている。
lines.english: As I tidied up, Watarai seemed to remember something and came to stand before me.

lines.japanese: 「今日？　って何かあったっけ？」
lines.english: “Today? Was something happening?”

lines.japanese: 「ううん、なにかあるわけじゃないんだけど……」
lines.english: “No, nothing in particular...”

lines.japanese: 渡来さんはちょっと目線を斜め上に泳がせたあと、軽く息を吸った。
lines.english: Watarai let her gaze drift diagonally upward for a moment, then drew a small breath.

lines.japanese: 「この前のやり直ししない？」
lines.english: “Want to take another shot at the other day?”

lines.japanese: 「この前の？」
lines.english: “The other day?”

lines.japanese: 「ほら昨日、一緒にゲームショップ寄ってくれるって言ったよね」
lines.english: “You said yesterday you’d stop by the game store with me, remember?”
“What? Oh...”

lines.japanese: 「今日はどう？」
lines.english: “How about today?”

lines.japanese: 世界は金色に輝いている。僕は飛びあがって歓喜の叫びをあげたかったけど、平静を装って答えた。
lines.english: The world shone gold. I wanted to leap into the air and shout for joy, but I pretended to be calm and answered.

lines.japanese: 「うん、まあ、平気だよ」
lines.english: “Yeah, well, I’m fine with that.”

lines.japanese: 「ほんと？　やった、よーし、じゃあ行こう」
lines.english: “Really? Yes! All right, let’s go.”

lines.japanese: まるでグレタガルドのように都合のいい世界。
lines.english: A world as obliging as Gretagard.

lines.japanese: 無防備に距離を詰めてくる渡来さんに心のどこかで違和感を覚えながら、しかし僕はあまりにも恋の甘さに溺れていて、ただ純粋に胸をときめかせていた。
lines.english: Somewhere inside, I felt a flicker of unease at the unguarded way Watarai closed the distance between us. But I was drowning in the sweetness of love, and my heart simply raced with innocent delight.

lines.japanese: 昨日なくした昂ぶりが蘇ってきて、昇降口まで渡来さんと交わした会話はまるで覚えていなかった。
lines.english: The exhilaration I had lost yesterday came flooding back. I could not remember a word Watarai and I exchanged on the way to the school entrance.

lines.japanese: だって、どうしようもなく楽しかったんだ。
lines.english: I was simply, helplessly happy.
